column1: # The Switch 2 leaves games 9 GB of its 12 GB. The NPDM declares 48 MB of system resource.
# 8 GB alias region stops OptimizeChangeBanc thread freeze in Kokiri Forest.
# Android: the host's frame limiter's default is 60 fps, the game's own top rate (the launcher's Frame rate cap, 60 / 45 / 40 / 30 / 20, and DM_FPS_LIMIT override it). Until
# 2026-11-11 it was 30: Link's house ran 37-38 fps from cool and 27-32 once hot, the phone 23 C warmer over a run; at 30 every frame is 33.3 ms and it warms 12 C (README.md
# "Profile"). The maintainer chose the game's own rate as the start; 30 is one tap away in the in-game panel
# Android: two pixel shaders whose draws later drawing covers (a sky-like layer: 6 draws of the first and 2 of the second cost 34 of 77 ms of GPU time at Link's house on an
# Adreno 740 with Turnip). The launcher's Game settings offer "Speedhack: Turn off hidden layers (experimental)" for them (DM_VK_SKIP_FS), off by default: judged by eye in
# Kokiri Forest and Link's house only
# The frame step (patches.py) in whole vsyncs decided by the host, also with no limit (the launcher's 60): left to the game's own controller, the game kept interval 1 at 25 fps on the
# phone (0.4 of real time; its controller's frame costs, framework +0x148 / +0x150, said 60 fits). The limit above caps the step (hle_fpslock.c dm_fps_step_fold): 30 fps = 2 vsyncs a frame
# The window crop the scene is upscaled into follows the operation mode and the Switch 2 graphics scale, not a window getter (README, Render size): the display state
# (main+0x6502e0) takes the scale from oe::GetCurrentGraphicsScale (main+0xe376d8) and picks the crop from a size table (main+0x112c5e0, as Mario Kart World):
# handheld scale 0 or 1 1920x1080, scale 2 1280x720 where the handheld parameters allow it; console scale 1 2560x1440 (at most: the crop is also capped by the mode's
# base size times the scale's factor, 2048x1152 on Mario Kart World). The Android launcher's Resolution sets these (res_preset rows; Advanced › Window). Phone 1440p and Original are console scale 1,
# the console's own docked picture (console mode: the game reports a docked controller and runs its scale-1-only passes). 540p and 480p have no row: no mode and scale
# goes below 1280x720, so they take the smallest row, 1280x720 (Profile.resolutionEnv)
# 3D scene (dm/tools/scene_res.py, README.md "Render size"): below the window crop the scene is a level of the game's own dynamic resolution palette, ModelSceneExtensionParam's
# DynamicResolutionParam in Pack/Bootup.Nin_Ounce_NVN2.pack.zs (zstd, pack.zsdic): 10 ResolutionReduceScale words for v131072, shared by both palettes (ResolutionParam: base
# and final 1920x1080, and 2560x1440 twice). The pack step writes one RomFS overlay per scene_scale row and per res_preset row with a floor or fixed scene, from the player's
# files; the launcher passes the chosen one as DM_ROMFS_OVERLAY
# The scene is the window's upscaler output times the scale. Both outputs measured on the phone (2026-11-12, res-auto-1112, system driver and Turnip V39, the host's
# 'NDSR upscaler replaced by SGSR 1: <in> -> <out>' line): handheld scale 0 crop 1920x1080, level 0 (0.75) 1440x810 and the 360p overlay (0.3125) 640x360; handheld scale 2
# crop 1280x720, performance (0.75) 960x540 and max-performance (0.5) 640x360, so the scale multiplies the window's own output, not the 1920x1080 base. Not 2048x1152: the
# fork's 1275x717 is 2048x1152 x the game's own 0.62223, likely a docked run (console scale 1). The console rows have no output row: no preset uses them
# Resolution presets (the launcher's one Resolution setting; the first row is the default, today's start): window and 3D scene together. Scales from the outputs above:
# balanced floor 720/1080 = 0.666667 (the game's own levels 0.75, 0.71112 and 0.66667 stay, the lower ones are raised to it), performance 540/720 = 0.75, max-performance
# 360/720 = 0.5. Max resolution (DM_OOT_MAX_RESOLUTION) takes the controller's full-scale path: meant for Quality (whether it still reads the palette is open)
# Recommended settings (dm/games/README.md "Recommended settings"), from the phone measurements in README.md "Recommended settings on Qualcomm phones" (2026-11-12, Adreno 840,
# Kokiri Forest): the phone's own Qualcomm driver draws this game 1.5-2x faster than Turnip; Performance and Full vegetation off take 3.7 and 1.6 ms off a 42.7 ms GPU frame
# (README.md "Recommended settings on Qualcomm phones": Performance and Full vegetation off, the settings that change this game's frame time there)
# Advanced › 3D scene (testers): fixed scales, labelled by scale (the launcher adds the size at the Advanced window where it has an output row). Names kept from before the
# presets: a stored choice keeps working (ResPresets.current maps it to a preset where one matches)
# agl wraps its clears in render conditions on Donkey Kong Bananza and Splatoon Raiders; the same library here

# As Tears of the Kingdom: the terrain's height, blend and hole maps are written by the CPU into textures after they are created. Without these keys they stay zero: holes in the ground and the wrong materials
# Foliage (Android, Qualcomm's driver): the depth-only prepass mesh draws come out as white spikes (a driver fault, cause open: README.md "Open"; docs/reference/rendering.md
# "Depth-only mesh prepass drawn as spikes on Qualcomm's driver"). They are not drawn; the colour pass draws their depth first with its own mesh module and the prepass's pixel
# shader (alpha cut-out), whose inputs move to where that module writes the same values. <prepass mesh> <colour mesh> <prepass location>:<colour location>,...
# The rows below are generated: dm/gfx/tools/mesh_prepass_pairs.py pairs the variation 2 mesh shader (the depth prepass) of every four-variation BNSH with its variation 0 (the colour
# pass): Foliage.Product.110 and ApplicationPackage's Foliage.Nin_Ounce_NVN2.bfsha; it maps them by running both Android mesh modules on the same random inputs (positions equal, then each output
# location matched). Locations left out (0: the prepass's dissolve factor, no colour output has it) read (0, 0, 0, 1): no dissolve, the plain cut-out.
# A row acts only on a depth-only draw into the depth image its colour mesh's EQUAL draws test against (vka_draw.c mesh_cut); rows the game never draws so do nothing
# mesh_prepass_pairs.py rows (dm/gfx/tools/mesh_prepass_pairs.py): generated, do not edit by hand
# Optional lower vegetation detail. Each pair was checked for guest-memory writes.
